statement: The big square is made of 36 equal small squares. What is the area of the shaded square, measured in small squares?

figure.alt: A 6 by 6 grid of small squares. A tilted shaded square has one corner on each side of the big square, each 2 small squares along from a corner of the big square. This leaves four white corner triangles, each with a short side of 2 and a long side of 4 along the edges of the big square.

choices.misconception: I took away four whole 2 by 4 rectangles instead of four triangles that are each half of one.
I counted only the small squares that lie completely inside the shaded square.
I found the total area of the four white corner triangles instead of the shaded square.
I treated each corner triangle as half of a 2 by 2 square, which made the triangles too small.

hints: Look at the white parts instead of the shaded part.
The shaded area is the big square minus the four white corner triangles. Each white triangle is half of a rectangle you can see on the grid.
Each white triangle is half of a 2 by 4 rectangle, so it covers 4 small squares.

solutions.reliable: The big square covers 36 small squares. Each white corner triangle is half of a 2 by 4 rectangle, so it covers 8 divided by 2 = 4. The four triangles cover 16. The shaded square covers 36 - 16 = 20 small squares. The transferable idea: when a shape is awkward, find the easy area around it and subtract.

whyOnTest: A tilted shape cannot be counted square by square, so it tests whether you think to subtract the pieces around it.
author: Devansh Sanghavi
